vulnerability_analysis: The WEB3 contract has an owner-only function setMaxTxPercent that can set _maxTxAmount. When set to 0, the _transfer function will require amount <= 0 for any transfer where neither sender nor recipient is the owner. Since amount must be > 0, this creates a contradiction that prevents all non-owner transfers, effectively locking user funds.
attack_strategy: Impersonate the contract owner, call setMaxTxPercent(0) to set _maxTxAmount to zero, then demonstrate that regular users cannot transfer tokens while the owner still can.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Get the current owner address of the WEB3 contract. 2. Use vm.prank to impersonate the owner. 3. Call setMaxTxPercent(0) on the WEB3 contract. 4. Create a test user address and transfer some tokens to it from the owner. 5. Attempt to transfer tokens from the test user to another address (should fail). 6. Verify that the owner can still transfer tokens (bypasses the _maxTxAmount check).
